etymology: From the Latin transcribere, to copy across - the written version of a thing that was said out loud.
effect: Converts a performance into a text, and a text into something you can quote back.
costs: Time, and the risk that your quote is worse out of context than it was in it.
failure: The transcript that is still being finalised, and the correction that quietly changes a word.
tell: A speaker label on every line

confused_with.tell: The request gets what the body wrote down; the transcript is what it said before anybody wrote it down.

senses: The verbatim record: what was said, in order, with who said it. Cheap to produce now and still the only artefact that settles an argument about what somebody said on Tuesday.

It works because a text can be searched and a performance cannot. The clip is chosen by whoever edits it; the transcript is chosen by whoever reads it - and that difference is the whole of the remedy.
example: *"The clip was everywhere by noon, and the **transcript** showed that the sentence had begun eleven seconds earlier, in a conditional."*
